title: Beatrix and the Veil
premise: Edmund Underhill's quiet life selling outlawed charms collapses when the crown's witch-hunt forces him to flee with Beatrix Vane, a disgraced inquisitor who secretly carries the last spark of dragon-fire. Their journey to the Veil—the shattered boundary between the human realm and the dragons' dying world—reveals that the covenant was broken not by dragons but by Edmund's own temple, which has been harvesting dragon-fire to fuel the crown's power. Betrayed by his temple and hunted by his oldest friend, Edmund must choose between restoring his own stolen reputation and telling a truth that will burn the temple down. In the end, he reforges the covenant at terrible cost: Beatrix gives her fire to relight the Veil, and Edmund, now its mortal keeper, chooses loyalty to truth over every institution that raised him.
about_author: Wendell Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, oaths, and the people trapped between them.

chapters.title: The Price of Small Wonders
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In the magic-outlawed city of Corvane, scribe Edmund sells harmless charms from a back-alley stall, hiding his gift behind temple paperwork. When a child's charm visibly works in public, Edmund realizes the crown's new hunt has informants everywhere. The beat is dread disguised as routine—the moment invisibility stops being safety.

chapters.title: A Visitor in Grey
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Disgraced inquisitor Beatrix Vane arrests Edmund but quietly lets him go, revealing she was once a fire-keeper of the old covenant—and that she carries the last living dragon-fire inside her scarred hands. She asks for his help reaching the Veil. The beat is wary alliance born of mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: What the Temple Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Returning to destroy his records, Edmund discovers the temple's sealed vaults humming with harvested dragon-fire, feeding the crown's engines. His mentor, Archivist Loewen, catches him and offers protection in exchange for silence. The beat is corrupted inheritance—learning his own house built the hunt.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Corvane
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Fleeing the city as the hunt begins in earnest, Beatrix narrates their escape through the salt marshes, where her fire flares and nearly betrays them. She tests Edmund's motives, convinced every scribe serves the temple first. The beat is grudging trust forged under pursuit.

chapters.title: Ashes of the First Oath
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At a ruined covenant-station, Edmund reads the original charter and learns the truth: the temple broke the pact first, siphoning fire for a century while blaming the dragons. He must decide whether to tell Beatrix that her order died protecting a lie. The beat is the weight of truth versus kindness.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Captain Ilsa Renn, Edmund's childhood friend and now the hunt's commander, corners them at a mountain pass—but hesitates, having seen what the harvested fire does to soldiers. She lets them pass with a warning. The beat is loyalty strained until it cracks; mercy as betrayal of one's own side.

chapters.title: Where the Fire Sleeps
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Reaching the Veil, they find it nearly dark, guarded by the last dragon, Vessarath, ancient and half-starved on memory alone. The dragon demands a price for renewal: a keeper bound in flesh and oath. The beat is awe curdling into terror at what restoration actually costs.

chapters.title: Loewen's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The temple's forces arrive, led by Loewen, who offers Edmund full pardon and restored standing if he surrenders Beatrix and the fire. Edmund refuses publicly, burning his temple credentials with a thread of Beatrix's flame. The beat is the protagonist's decisive break from corrupt power.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Battle at the Veil: Ilsa turns her soldiers against Loewen, but the fighting shatters the boundary's anchor stone. Beatrix pours her entire fire into the breach to hold it open, knowing it will consume her. The beat is sacrifice as climax—loyalty to a truth worth dying for.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Veil
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The covenant is reforged: the Veil burns steady, dragons return to the far side, and Beatrix survives diminished, mortal, freed of her burden. Edmund accepts the keeper's oath, exiled from the city he saved. The beat is bittersweet resolution—inheritance reclaimed as responsibility, not reward.
